promise: Every episode takes one question a foreigner would actually ask about Korea and answers it with evidence you can see on screen - and tells you why it made sense to the people back then.

personas.name: Korea-curious (English-speaking)
personas.korea_knowledge: near zero history; knows Korea through K-drama, K-pop, food or one trip
personas.entry_point: K-drama / travel to Seoul or Gyeongju / K-pop / Korean friends
wants: understand what they saw or heard ("why is that there?")
a clear answer in under 10 minutes, no lecture tone
to feel the people were real, not a museum label
misconceptions: all old Korean things are 'Joseon' / hanbok = one look
ancient Korea was poor and simple
frictions: unclear what is fact vs guess

personas.name: History-documentary regular
personas.korea_knowledge: some world history; Korea is a gap
misconceptions: Korean history starts with the Korean War

core_questions: Why are giant grass mounds in the middle of a Korean city?
Why did Silla make gold crowns - who wore them?
Why do Koreans heat the floor instead of the room?
Is this Korean or Chinese or Japanese? (how to tell)

needs_map.need: make sense of something seen in Korea
needs_map.we_answer_with: ① QUESTION from the present-day view + ⑦ LEGACY back to today

needs_map.need: know what is fact and what is a guess
needs_map.we_answer_with: FACT / INTERPRETIVE labels on screen, sources in description
⑤ MINDSET AI reenactment, 5-6 s cuts, ~10% of runtime (D-033 #3)
③ FACT with GT-01~04 diagrams and on-screen dimensions

differentiators: The question comes first, and it is the question a foreigner asks - not the one a Korean textbook asks.
Fact and interpretation are separated on screen (labels, hedged narration, sources in the description).
The people of the past appear as real people (Documentary Reenactment style B, Character Master), not as spectacle.

cadence.note: D-046: 격주 토 14:00 UTC (미국 아침·유럽 오후). EP01 게시일은 P-012·편집 뒤 확정.

cta_policy.description_cta: One CTA only, after the Sources block: subscribe for the next question.
cta_policy.pinned_comment_cta: One question to viewers: what would you have asked standing here? (question harvesting input)
